items.title: As the ceasefire cracks, Iran gets 'a complete reset' of the pressure on its oil trade
items.description: The ceasefire between the United States and Iran is fraying and Washington has attempted to crush the regime's oil sales, but Tehran made its move when the blockade lifted weeks ago.

items.title: When politics becomes content the risks multiply
items.description: Every press conference, reel and podcast is now a chance for politicians to connect with voters. Yet the strategy that broadens an MP's reach can also amplify their biggest mistakes.

items.title: India a 'top-tier' security partner for Australia as nations deepen defence ties
items.description: Anthony Albanese says Australia will increase coordination with India's military forces following talks with the nation's Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Melbourne.

items.title: ABC's editorial director says delay to on-air correction a 'bad mistake'
items.description: The ABC's editorial director Gavin Fang tells a royal commission it was a "bad mistake" an on-air correction about a statement on Gaza was not made on the same program the error first occurred.

items.title: Breaking: Death on day of Telstra outage investigated by police
items.description: Police in SA are investigating a death at a regional South Australian hospital yesterday, after Liberal Senator Kerrynne Liddle said an elderly person had died during the Telstra outage.

items.title: This nursery owner doesn't use Telstra, but the outage still cost her dearly
items.description: The economic cost of the latest Telstra network outage could run into hundreds of millions of dollars, an expert estimates.

items.title: 'Pretty cool': Trump announces win for Ukraine amid fiery NATO meeting
items.description: Donald Trump says his country will probably continue to attack Iran and says Ukraine will be given permission to manufacture much-needed Patriot missiles as it fights Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: 'Cannot remain silent': Egypt demands FIFA investigate World Cup referees
items.description: Egypt remains incensed at French referee Francois Letexier after his performance in the Round of 16 clash against Argentina at the FIFA World Cup.

items.title: Neil the seal may have left Tasmania, wildlife experts say
items.description: Authorities in Tasmania say it appears Neil the seal may have left his resting spot at a Hobart beach and returned to sea.

items.title: Search for crew continues after Boeing cargo plane crash
items.description: Rescue crews battle rough sea conditions to recover parts of a Boeing cargo plane that crashed into the Arabian Sea. Five crew members remain missing.

items.title: NSW Police officer taken into custody after sexually assaulting then-wife
items.description: A NSW Police officer has been taken into custody after his bail was revoked by a judge, two days after he was found guilty of choking and sexually assaulting his then-wife.

items.title: State of Origin decider breaks broadcast record
items.description: An unprecedented number of viewers tuned into the State of Origin decider, in which NSW stunned Queensland to win the series.

items.title: Court told former Wagga Wagga MP was 'kept in dark' over visa scheme
items.description: Daryl Maguire's barrister has told a jury it was "unbelievable" to think the ex NSW MP would recruit people in his electorate to take part in an allegedly fraudulent visa scheme.

items.title: Growers push to overturn ban on ancient 'superfood'
items.description: Farmers are appealing against a federal ban on the sale of Moringa oleifera as a food after a regulatory body determined there was insufficient evidence to prove its safety.

items.title: This Place: Koala Brother, Yarriabini
items.description: Uncle Micklo Jarrett is a Gumbaynggirr man, sharing a dreamtime story about how Yarriabini mountain, on the mid north coast of New South Wales, got its name. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: The grief of childlessness will always be with me
items.description: The grief of losing the chance to have baby is something I expect to carry forever. But I'm becoming more comfortable with the unconventional life I'm building with my partner April.

items.title: TV catchphrase quiz: Guess the show from the famous quote
items.description: Now for the story of 20 famous TV quotes, and the one quiz that had no choice but to keep them all together.

items.title: 'Important' Aboriginal language statement released amid 'abysmal' loss
items.description: Aboriginal language custodians release a road map for the survival and revival of Northern Territory Indigenous languages.

items.title: Water in the air an 'untapped water resource' until now
items.description: Can water be made from air in WA's Wheatbelt? Researchers are putting an invention to the test.

items.title: Swimming Australia fights 'scary' fake news in world-first initiative
items.description: In a world-first initiative, Swimming Australia is taking a proactive approach to deal with clickbait and fake news headlines about its athletes, including Olympic champion Mollie O'Callaghan, who has been targeted in the past.

items.title: Gout Gout ruled out of World Under-20 athletics titles after training injury
items.description: Australian athletics star Gout Gout is ruled out of this year's World Under-20 titles in Oregon after a training injury in Brisbane.

items.title: FIFA boss referred to Olympics ethics board over Trump World Cup call
items.description: Gianni Infantino's close ties with Donald Trump continue to land him in hot water after the US President's World Cup intervention.

items.title: Man, 34, charged with murder over death of girl, 17
items.description: Days after a 17-year-old girl was found dead inside a home in the remote community of Galiwin'ku, police have charged a 34-year-old man following an autopsy.

items.title: The key ingredient keeping the snow season alive
items.description: Data shows snow depth has been declining in Australia since the 1950s, with resorts turning to snowmaking to guarantee a strong ski season.

items.title: 'Going to make it double': Boxer's jokes about domestic violence condemned
items.description: A leading violence prevention organisation says an Australian boxer's joke about domestic violence is unacceptable.
